item.title: India-US trade deal ‘much different’: As Marco Rubio meets Jaishankar in Mumbai, here's what Trump said
item.description: US President Donald Trump said the US and India are close to finalising a trade deal after more than a year of negotiations. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the agreement could materialise within weeks, as both sides work through the final technical and legal details.
item.dc:creator: Akriti Anand
item.content:encoded: US President Donald Trump said on Tuesday that the US and India are close to finalising a trade deal after more than a year of negotiations. His statement came as US Secretary of State Marco Rubio met External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar in Mumbai on Tuesday.“They want to make a deal. We’re going to make a deal. Pretty close, yeah,” Trump was quoted by Bloomberg as saying on Tuesday when asked by reporters at the White House about the prospects for an agreement.The president said it “could be a much different kind of deal,” without elaborating.Deal to ‘materialise in a matter of weeks, not months’Trump's remarks came amid US Secretary of State Marco Rubio's visit to India this week.Marco Rubio is on an official visit to India from October 20 to 21 at the invitation of External Affairs Minister Jaishankar, marking his second visit to the country following an earlier trip to New Delhi in May.At the Freedom 250 reception in Mumbai, Rubio also revealed that the India-US trade deal is “incredibly close”, indicating that finalisation is anticipated shortly, news agency ANI reported.Speaking to Network18, Rubio noted that while he is not directly engaged in the negotiations, which are handled through the trade representative, he has closely monitored the discussions and expects the agreement to materialise in a matter of weeks, not months.Elaborating on the final stages, Rubio highlighted the need for absolute precision before public announcements to safeguard the bilateral ties of such high importance.He said, “I felt that way before, and with these deals, it’s always important that it would be totally agreed to, every detail of it, before it’s announced because you can’t afford for a relationship of this magnitude to be threatened by announcing a deal and it turning out the deal wasn’t finalised.""But it’s incredibly close. I think we are down to some technical details that need to be worked out. Technical details matter because there has to be an agreement; both sides have to agree that the language means the same thing. So, it’s down to that level,” he was quoted as saying.India and US on trade dealBoth US and Indian officials have recently made optimistic comments about the chances of an agreement, which would break a long-running stalemate over trade between Washington and New Delhi.US Ambassador to India Sergio Gor said last week at the Bloomberg New Economy Forum in New Delhi that “the big items are done” and that the two countries are very close to “landing it”.That followed remarks by Indian External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar in which he said he was encouraged by progress in trade talks and that both sides were “heading toward a landing point.”Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal had also said the "first tranche" of the deal would be finalised soon."It's going through the final contours, the legal drafting, and we hope to be able to finalise that soon and operationalise that once we get comparable advantage or competitive advantage over our peer countries," a statement from his office quoted him as saying at an event in New Delhi.According to Reuters, Goyal was referring to New Delhi's efforts to secure a tariff advantage for Indian exporters over competing economies such as Bangladesh, Vietnam and Indonesia in the US market.Trump late Friday waived tariffs of as much as 100% on buyers of Russian oil and gas — duties that would have hit Indian products and complicated trade negotiations.US targets $500 bn bilateral trade with India in three yearsUS Ambassador to India Sergio Gor said recently that the US has set an ambitious target to double its bilateral trade with India to over $500 billion within the next three years, up from a record-breaking $240 billion.Addressing business leaders and diplomats at the Freedom 250 reception in Mumbai, Ambassador Gor highlighted the deepening economic and strategic partnership between the two nations.He noted that President Donald Trump sent him to India with a clear mandate -- "Deliver results. Don't just talk about the future. Make it happen.""In their recent discussions, President Trump and Prime Minister Modi reaffirmed that commitment," Gor was quoted by ANI as saying.He said, "Today, our bilateral trade has shattered records, reaching over $240 billion. We have an ambitious goal. We are laser-focused on driving that number past $500 billion in the next three years."

item.title: Nigeria Ebola Case Widens Record Outbreak Across Africa
item.description: Nigeria’s first Ebola infection in more than a decade is widening an outbreak that already spread to several African countries, prompting the continent’s top public-health agency to call for urgent international assistance.
item.dc:creator: list.metadata.agency
item.content:encoded: (Bloomberg) -- Nigeria’s first Ebola infection in more than a decade is widening an outbreak that already spread to several African countries, prompting the continent’s top public-health agency to call for urgent international assistance.The Nigerian case was caused by the Bundibugyo strain, Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention Director-General Jean Kaseya said in a statement on Tuesday. The agency is mobilizing support for Nigeria, while intensifying its response in the Democratic Republic of Congo and Kenya, he said.“This Ebola Bundibugyo outbreak has already become the most geographically widespread Ebola outbreak in history, affecting multiple countries across three regions of Africa,” Kaseya said.Nigeria previously confirmed that a woman who recently arrived in the country on a flight from Uganda had tested positive for the virus. She began showing symptoms on Oct. 7 and was admitted to a private hospital in Abuja on Oct. 11, according to Health Minister Muhammad Ali Pate. She is now in isolation and receiving medical care.Authorities have identified 44 of her contacts so far and are tracing and monitoring people who may have been exposed, including healthcare workers, patients, caregivers and travel contacts.“We are doing everything possible to contain this case by tracing all the contacts the individual may have had,” Pate said.Nigeria, the continent’s most populous nation, is a major West African travel hub.Bundibugyo has no approved vaccines or therapies. Moderna Inc. has begun testing an experimental vaccine designed to target the virus. The Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations, a nonprofit focused on developing new vaccines for pandemic threats, is helping fund the effort.The current outbreak began more than five months ago in Congo, which has recorded 9,552 confirmed infections and 4,602 deaths, according to the National Institute of Public Health. The crude case-fatality rate is 48%.Uganda recorded cases earlier in the outbreak and remains on heightened alert, while Kenya has reported infections linked to a traveler from Congo who passed through Uganda before arriving in Nairobi. Patients with infections tied to the outbreak have also been detected or treated in Europe.Africa CDC called for immediate international financing, medical supplies, diagnostics, trained responders and stronger community-based surveillance to prevent further spread.“We cannot allow this outbreak to spread to more countries or continue for another year,” Kaseya said. “Every day of delay costs lives.”The last Ebola outbreak reported in Nigeria was in 2014, when an infected traveler arrived in Lagos from Liberia during the West African Ebola epidemic.--With assistance from Jessica Nix.(Updates with Africa CDC comment from first paragraph)More stories like this are available on bloomberg.com©2026 Bloomberg L.P.
